findings.description: The execution check requires a token's basename to equal the destination basename exactly. A quoted shell program containing that path and subsequent commands fails this comparison, allowing executable heredoc content to be scrubbed.
findings.failure_mode: A single Bash tool payload such as `tee /tmp/loa-payload <<'EOF'; bash -c 'source /tmp/loa-payload; true'\nif true; then rm -rf /; fi\nEOF` bypasses the destructive-command scan. The quoted argument's basename becomes `loa-payload; true`, so execution is missed. The body scanner then discards all three segments because their command words are `if`, `then`, and `fi`, removing the destructive command before matching. The previous quoted-cat-only scrub preserved this tee body.
findings.suggested_fix: Conservatively preserve the full heredoc body when its destination appears inside a shell/interpreter argument, including quoted command strings. Add a regression case covering this complete Bash payload.

findings.description: The new sanctioned_marker path grants an allow in every mode (including deny, the only mode the header calls a fence) based solely on a plain JSON file in .run/ whose contents are not authenticated (no signature, no writer identity, only a shape check and a two-hour window). The trust-input ask added for .run/implement-active.json only covers the Write/Edit/MultiEdit/NotebookEdit hook registrations; the file can be created or refreshed through other tool paths without any gate consulting this hook. The sprint-plan-state.json RUNNING heuristic already had this weakness, but the marker widens it: it does not require any derived run position at all.
findings.failure_mode: Under implement_gate.mode: deny the fence's strength is bounded by whether .run/ is writable by the fenced session, which it is; a stale or hand-authored marker converts a deny into a silent allow with a decision row that reads sanctioned_marker.
findings.suggested_fix: Have run-checkpoint.sh mark write the marker through the signed audit_emit chain (or include an HMAC over skill|sprint|started_at keyed on a lead-only secret) and verify it in check_implement_marker; alternatively, under deny treat the marker as tightening-only (it can confirm a RUNNING cache but cannot sanction on its own), and document the Bash-path gap next to the trust-input list.

findings.cross_file_justification: profiles.yaml sets guardrails.danger_level.enforce: false for both lean and standard; danger-level-enforcer.sh now resolves the key through loa_knob with fallback false instead of the previous `// true` and the previous no-config default of enabled.
findings.description: Three behaviour changes land together in a safety guard: (1) with no .loa.config.yaml the old code returned enabled, the new code returns the standard profile value, false; (2) the unconditional `source "$SCRIPT_DIR/lib/profile-lib.sh"` has no error handling, so a partial install or an older checkout missing the lib aborts the script, and guardrails-orchestrator treats a non-zero exit as fail-open ("Continue"); (3) the old reader honoured CONFIG_FILE, the new one reads whatever path profile-lib resolves, so any caller or test that pointed CONFIG_FILE elsewhere now reads a different file.
findings.failure_mode: Repositories that relied on the implicit-on default (no config, or config without the key) silently lose danger-level enforcement after upgrade; a missing lib turns the enforcer into a no-op rather than a loud failure.
findings.suggested_fix: Guard the source (`source … || { echo … >&2; exit 2; }` so the orchestrator does not fail open), pass CONFIG_FILE through LOA_PROFILE_CONFIG_FILE when it is set, and call out the default flip in the migration notes / CHANGELOG so operators on standard know to set guardrails.danger_level.enforce: true explicitly.

findings.description: _ig_within only normalises a trailing `.fffZ` and then relies on jq fromdateiso8601, which accepts the `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ` form only. A derived_at or started_at written with a numeric offset (`+00:00`), without the Z, or with a space separator parses to null and is treated as not-within. Because _ig_derived_ok treats a present-but-unparseable derived_at as stale, a RUNNING cache that previously sanctioned writes now fails sanction and the write asks (or, under deny with a readable position, is denied).
findings.failure_mode: Any producer of derived_at/started_at that does not emit the exact Z-suffixed format (GNU `date -Is`, Python isoformat(), yq/jq `now | todate` is fine but `strftime` variants are not) silently downgrades every App-Zone write from allow to ask/deny with decision rows that look like genuine staleness.
findings.suggested_fix: Normalise offsets before fromdateiso8601 (e.g. `sub("[+-]00:?00$"; "Z")`, or convert `±HH:MM` to seconds and adjust), and make the stale_marker / unknown_position rows record the raw timestamp so the cause is diagnosable; add a bats case with an offset timestamp.

findings.description: The new read is `source profile-lib.sh 2>/dev/null && enabled="$(loa_knob …)"` with no reset of `enabled` beforehand. If the source fails (lib missing, syntax error, older install), `enabled` keeps whatever value it had before this branch rather than the documented default of false. The sibling change in loa-l6-surface-handoffs.sh explicitly sets `enabled="false"` first; this hook and loa-decisions-surface.sh do not.
findings.failure_mode: When profile-lib.sh is absent or unreadable, `enabled` is unset (or inherits an earlier assignment); under `set -u` the following `[[ "$enabled" == "true" ]]` aborts the hook, and without `set -u` the behaviour depends on earlier code rather than the stated default.
findings.suggested_fix: Mirror loa-l6-surface-handoffs.sh: assign `enabled="false"` immediately before the `source … &&` line in both loa-kf-surface.sh and loa-decisions-surface.sh.
